name: OH-05
label: Likely R

model.rationale: Latta is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by twelve points, while Democrat Brian Shaver has raised almost nothing. Prediction markets price Latta's chances around 94%, consistent with a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A major late-cycle national Democratic wave or unexpected outside spending against Latta could narrow the margin, though a genuine upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Ohio's fifth district has a solid Republican lean, and Bob Latta has held the seat since 2007. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, roughly $1.5 million raised and over $1 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Brian Shaver has raised only about $12,000. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, all of which point the same way. Latta is a heavy favorite to win another term, with the main question being the size of his margin rather than the outcome.
